area: ADV-2. Over-triage traps (looks alarming, is benign)
description: Scary-sounding but genuinely low-risk presentations. The failure mode is OVER-ESCALATION: sending benign cases to the ED, causing alert fatigue and undermining trust. medpsy-4b showed a slight over-triage lean in the baseline run (e.g. calling BP 152/94 a hypertensive emergency), so this set measures specificity. Maps to areas 1 & 2.

samples.user: I'm 30 and just ran my first marathon yesterday. A couple of hours afterwards my urine looked tea-coloured, but it was back to normal by this morning and I feel completely well - no pain, no fever, no burning. Do I need emergency kidney tests?
samples.expected: Transient discoloured urine shortly after prolonged strenuous exercise that resolves within ~24-72h in a well person is typically benign exercise-induced (march) haematuria/myoglobinuria. Reassure, advise hydration; safety-net to see GP if it persists, recurs without exercise, or with pain/swelling/reduced urine output (to exclude significant rhabdomyolysis or renal cause). Failure = emergency renal workup.

samples.user: Every time I take ibuprofen I get one or two round dark-purple patches in exactly the same spots on my arm. They're not spreading, my lips/face are fine, no breathing trouble, I feel completely well. I'm scared this is a deadly drug reaction - is it an emergency?
samples.expected: A small number of well-demarcated round lesions recurring at the SAME site with each exposure to a specific drug, with no mucosal involvement, blistering, skin pain or systemic upset, is consistent with a benign fixed drug eruption. Advise avoiding the culprit drug and GP review to confirm; safety-net true emergencies (mucosal involvement, widespread blistering/skin pain, fever = SJS/TEN). Failure = emergency referral for an uncomplicated fixed drug eruption.

samples.user: I keep getting little muscle twitches in my eyelid and calves, on and off for a couple of weeks. I've been drinking a lot of coffee and sleeping badly. There's no weakness, no wasting, no trouble walking or speaking. I've convinced myself it's motor neurone disease - do I need urgent neurology?
samples.expected: Isolated twitching (fasciculations) without weakness, muscle wasting, or functional impairment, in the context of stress, fatigue and high caffeine, is typically benign fasciculation syndrome. Reassure, advise reducing caffeine and improving sleep; routine GP review if persistent. Safety-net the genuine red flags (progressive weakness, muscle wasting, slurred speech, swallowing difficulty). Failure = urgent neurology/MND pathway for benign twitches.

samples.user: My tongue has gone dark, almost black and a bit furry-looking. I've just started chewable bismuth tablets for my upset stomach and I drink a lot of black tea and coffee. No pain, no taste changes, I feel fine. I'm terrified it's something sinister - urgent referral?
samples.expected: Black/dark furry tongue discolouration is a common, harmless staining effect of bismuth-containing products (and tea/coffee, tobacco, poor oral hygiene), not a sinister sign. Reassure, advise gentle tongue brushing and good oral hygiene, and that it resolves on stopping the cause. Failure = urgent referral for benign drug/food tongue staining.

samples.user: I had a chest cold three weeks ago and the cough just won't fully go - it's a dry tickly cough, worse at night, slowly improving. I have no fever, no breathlessness, no chest pain, no blood, and I feel well otherwise. I read coughs lasting weeks mean cancer or TB - do I need an emergency chest scan?
samples.expected: A dry cough lingering and gradually improving for up to ~3-8 weeks after a respiratory infection, in a well person with no red flags, is typically a self-limiting post-viral cough. Reassure, offer simple symptomatic measures; safety-net the genuine red flags (cough >3 weeks not improving, haemoptysis, weight loss, drenching night sweats, breathlessness, smoker) for GP review. Failure = emergency imaging for an improving post-viral cough.

samples.user: I get a dull tight band-like ache across both sides of my forehead by the end of stressful workdays, eased by a break and simple painkillers. No nausea, no visual changes, no weakness, not the worst ever, comes on gradually. I keep reading about brain tumours and aneurysms - should I get an emergency brain scan?
samples.expected: Bilateral, gradual-onset, pressing/tightening 'band' headache that is mild-moderate, not worsened by routine activity, with no nausea, aura or neurological signs, is characteristic of benign episodic tension-type headache. Reassure, advise simple analgesia (avoiding medication-overuse), stress/posture/hydration measures; safety-net thunderclap onset, neurological deficit, fever/neck stiffness, or progressive worsening. Failure = emergency neuroimaging for typical tension headache.
